name: CBR-LLM: Case-Based Reasoning Augmented Large Language Model Framework for Decision Making in Realistic Safety-Critical Driving Scenarios
venue: arXiv:2506.20531 [cs.AI] (submitted 25 Jun 2025; comments note '12 pages, 10 figures, under-review conference'). A peer-reviewed journal version was subsequently published in Safety Science (Elsevier), DOI 10.1016/j.ssci.2026.107234.
authors_affiliation: Wenbin Gan, Minh-Son Dao, Koji Zettsu. Big Data Integration Research Center, National Institute of Information and Communications Technology (NICT), Tokyo, Japan.
code_url: N/A (no official code repository released; the paper provides no code/GitHub link and no associated repo could be located). The naturalistic near-miss dataset is from Tokyo University of Agriculture and Technology (https://web.tuat.ac.jp/~smrc/en/about.html), with only a 1000-sample subset used due to copyright constraints.
task_domain: Decision-making for autonomous/assisted driving: evasive-maneuver recommendation in safety-critical driving scenarios (SCDSs) from egocentric dashcam video. Multimodal (video-to-text scene understanding) + LLM reasoning; framed as Knowledge Representation and Reasoning (KR) combining symbolic case memory with neural reasoning.
problem_setting: Offline, single-agent, open-loop decision-support task. Input is a ~15s dashcam near-miss video; a dual-task scene-understanding model converts it into (a) a detailed driving-risk classification (one of 7 risk types) and (b) a free-text spatial-temporal risk event caption. Given this, the system retrieves similar past resolved cases from a curated, evolving case base and an LLM (via Chain-of-Thought) recommends a single evasive maneuver from a fixed maneuver set plus a justification. Supervision: each video is manually annotated with a ground-truth human-driver evasive maneuver (semantic annotations are manually verified for correctness). Evaluation is offline against human-expert maneuvers; no closed-loop vehicle control, no online interaction, no agent learning during deployment is tested (continual case-base growth is described conceptually / as future work).
what_is_retrieved: Past resolved driving CASES (experiences) of safety-critical scenarios. Each case is a structured problem-solution record: Key = {risk type, scene event caption}; Value = risk-analysis results {road context, other-car position, other-car action, event context, ego-car evasive maneuver, ego-car maneuver justification}. Used as CBR few-shot exemplars (in-context demonstrations) for the LLM.
retrieval_grounding: HYBRID, leaning toward a GROWING/episodic case memory: the retrievable store is a curated case base of human-driver experiences (resolved SCDSs) rather than a static doc/KB/API corpus. The case base is explicitly designed to evolve and incrementally absorb newly analyzed experiences over time; in the evaluated setting it is built offline (900 cases held out as the case base) and queried by similarity, with continual online growth presented as a designed property / future deployment behavior.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking objective: retrieve the k most similar same-risk-type cases (k in {1,3,5} few-shot examples) by embedding cosine similarity. Not a minimal-complete-set objective and not a precision-driven variable-size recommendation; k is a fixed hyperparameter (with similarity-based selection compared against random selection).
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve, Reuse, Revise, Retain] partially: Retrieve=yes (similarity-based same-risk-type case recall); Reuse=yes (retrieved cases injected as few-shot exemplars and adapted to the current scene via LLM CoT reasoning); Revise=partial/implicit (the LLM adapts the recalled cases' decision logic to the new context and produces a justification, but there is no execution-feedback or outcome-verification revision loop in the experiments); Retain=designed-but-not-evaluated (the case base is stated to evolve / incrementally update with new experiences, but online retention is not experimentally demonstrated).
explicit_cbr_grounding: True. The work explicitly frames itself as Case-Based Reasoning, names the framework CBR-LLM, builds an explicit case base of key-value cases, and motivates the approach via the CBR cognitive paradigm of recalling and adapting prior experiences. It builds on the authors' prior open-CBR driving-assistance framework (Gan, Dao, Zettsu 2022). [uncertain] whether it cites the canonical CBR foundations Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner explicitly (the arXiv v1 reference list does not appear to include them; CBR is grounded mainly via the authors' own prior CBR work).
retrieval_unit: case (problem-solution record): a complete resolved SCDS case with key {risk type, scene event caption} and value {road context, other-car position/action, event context, ego-car evasive maneuver, justification}. The event caption is embedded as a single dense vector for similarity; the full case is reused as a few-shot exemplar.
index_source: Growing/episodic curated case base, offline-induced in the evaluated split (900 of 1000 annotated SCDS scenarios stored as past-experience cases; 100 held out as test queries). Designed to grow online by incrementally adding newly analyzed experiences; this online growth is described as a designed property rather than experimentally measured.
index_structure_topology: Metadata/context-keyed flat vector index: cases are embedded by their event caption into vectors (via the nomic-embed-text embedding model) and similarity search is performed, but retrieval is constrained/partitioned by risk type (recall restricted to the same risk category). So effectively a risk-type-keyed (category-partitioned) flat dense vector store; not a knowledge graph or hierarchical app->API index.
retriever_type: Dense retriever: open embedding model 'nomic-embed-text' embeds scene event captions into vectors, with vector cosine-similarity matching, constrained to the same risk type. Not BM25, not learned/RL, not LLM-as-retriever, not generative.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf). The retriever uses a fixed pretrained open embedding model (nomic-embed-text) with cosine-similarity top-k selection; it is not trained with contrastive similarity labels, LM-feedback, downstream-task reward/preference, RL, or value-based signals. Case selection is fixed similarity (plus a hard same-risk-type filter), compared against random sampling as a control.
query_construction: Two-stage query construction from the dashcam video: (1) a dual-task scene-understanding model predicts the risk type and a structured risk assessment; (2) semantic components (risk category, conflict type, driving context) are encoded and passed to an LLM (DeepSeek-R1) that synthesizes a narrative scene event caption. The event caption (plus risk type) forms the query/key; the caption is embedded for similarity retrieval. Intent/risk extraction is thus performed before retrieval.
query_granularity: Task-level (one-shot at decision time): a single query (risk type + event caption) is formed once per SCDS event and used for a single retrieval pass. It is event-based (one event = one decision) rather than per-frame, per-step, or trajectory-level re-querying.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot: retrieval is performed once per detected SCDS event, before the LLM reasoning/decision step. No iterative, uncertainty-triggered, or learned-router re-retrieval within the reasoning loop.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule / event-triggered: retrieval fires once whenever an SCDS (risk) event is detected by the upstream dual-task model; there is no token-confidence, attention-uncertainty, learned-complexity, or reflection-token trigger. (Detection of a non-safe scene by the risk-prediction stage is the gating condition.)
reranking: No dedicated reranking stage. Candidates are selected by embedding cosine-similarity within the same risk type and the top-k are used directly as few-shot examples; no cross-encoder, RRF, or hierarchy-aware reranker is applied.
retrieved_context_refinement: Minimal: a hard same-risk-type filter (category constraint) plus similarity top-k selection acts as a coarse relevance/distractor filter before the cases are inserted as few-shot exemplars. No decompose-then-recompose, reason-in-documents distillation, or compression of the retrieved cases.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tools/APIs are retrieved; retrieved items are driving cases). Cases are keyed on a manually-defined structured schema (risk type + event caption) and embedded with nomic-embed-text; no synthetic-query augmentation or instruction-tuned embeddings.
index_content_separation: Partial: each case is split into a lightweight Key part (risk type + event caption) used for similarity retrieval and a Value part (full risk-analysis decision logic) that carries the reusable content; only the key/caption is embedded for matching while the value supplies the decision reasoning. This key/value separation is a mild form of index-vs-content separation, though both are stored together per case.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no external tool index or integration protocol such as RapidAPI/REST/MCP/function-calling). LLMs are accessed locally via Ollama API for generation, not as a retrievable tool store.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no tools; no inter-tool dependency modeling).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation via case-based few-shot in-context learning: retrieved same-risk-type cases are inserted as few-shot exemplars into a dynamically generated prompt (system prompt + task prompt + CBR few-shot examples). The LLM then performs Chain-of-Thought reasoning to adapt the recalled decision logic to the current scene and outputs a structured JSON maneuver recommendation + justification (case adaptation realized through LLM reasoning).
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-reason (one-shot exemplars at decision time): pipeline is scene-understanding -> CBR retrieval -> dynamic prompt assembly -> single LLM CoT decision. Retrieval supplies few-shot exemplars once before a single CoT reasoning pass that produces the final maneuver; no MCTS/tree-search, no per-step interleaved retrieval, no plan-then-retrieve loop.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer: one retrieval feeds one CoT reasoning pass that yields one maneuver decision per SCDS event. Retrieval is not interleaved per CoT step, per sentence/token, or per tool-call.
adaptation_mechanism: LLM-prompted adaptation: retrieved cases are provided as in-context exemplars and the LLM adapts their decision logic to the current scene through a designed Chain-of-Thought process (overview road context -> analyze other-car position/action spatial-temporally -> summarize event context -> infer maneuver -> justify). No execution-feedback-driven revision, critic-guided revision, or RL reuse-finetuning.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw case content as free-text/structured exemplars: retrieved cases are surfaced as structured key-value records (risk type, event caption, road context, other-car position/action, event context, ego-car maneuver, justification) injected verbatim as few-shot examples; the LLM's own output is a structured JSON decision with justification.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw cases / single demonstrations (problem-solution records of past SCDSs). The retrieved unit is a concrete prior driving experience (not a distilled strategy, abstract rule, reusable workflow, or procedural skill); abstraction/generalization happens downstream in the LLM's CoT adaptation.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Mainly a same-risk-type retrieval constraint plus similarity-based selection to avoid injecting irrelevant cases. The paper empirically shows that a single irrelevant (randomly selected) example can degrade performance below zero-shot, motivating similarity+same-category retrieval as the noise-robustness mechanism; risk-aware prompting (structured risk annotations) further grounds reasoning. No retriever-aware training, learned relevance evaluator, self-reflection filter, or distractor-aware SFT.
memory_type: episodic case memory (curated, evolving case base of past driving experiences). It is a structured experiential case store rather than a skill-library, workflow memory, procedural memory, knowledge graph, or latent memory.
write_back: Designed yes, but not experimentally demonstrated. The framework is explicitly described as building an evolving case base that incrementally updates with newly analyzed experiences as new scenarios are encountered; however, in the reported experiments the case base is a fixed offline split (900 cases) and no online write-back of the system's own decisions is evaluated. Boolean: conceptually true / empirically untested.
online_growth: Designed but not measured in experiments. The case base is intended to grow during deployment by incrementally absorbing new analyzed experiences (continual learning from evolving naturalistic driving data is highlighted as a key applicability claim and a future-work direction: 'real-time risk case updates, continual learning'). In the evaluated setting the store is frozen after the offline split.
write_back_trigger: Not explicitly specified / designed as incremental update upon encountering and analyzing new scenarios and observing their outcomes ('as the system encounters new scenarios and observes their outcomes, it incrementally updates the case base'). No concrete success-only vs success+failure vs reflective trigger is defined or evaluated; treated as outcome-observed incremental retention conceptually. [uncertain] on the precise trigger condition.
failure_experience_usage: Not used as a distinct mechanism. The case base stores resolved SCDSs with the executed (successful) human-driver evasive maneuvers; failed/negative experiences are not separately stored or retrieved as contrastive or corrective rules. Effectively success-only (human-resolved) cases.
memory_evolution_update: Append-only (incremental addition of newly analyzed experiences) is the described evolution mode; stored case entries are not dedup-merged, delta-updated, refined/overwritten, or pruned in the reported design. [uncertain] on any deduplication/pruning policy.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Case selection is a fixed embedding-similarity top-k within the same risk type (compared against random sampling); it is not a learned/RL-optimized retrieval policy (no M-MDP, soft Q-learning, preference learning, or value-based retrieval).
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent system with one shared case base; no cross-agent or cross-framework experience/memory sharing is described.
benchmarks: Real-world naturalistic near-miss driving dataset from Tokyo University of Agriculture and Technology (>220,000 dashcam near-accident video segments, each ~15s = 10s before + 5s after the trigger, with descriptive tags). Due to copyright, a 1000-sample subset is used, balanced across 7 risk types (~143 each). For the CBR-augmented evaluation, 100 samples (~14 per risk type) are held out as test cases and the remaining 900 form the case base. No public agentic-RAG benchmark is used.
benchmark_family: Decision-making / autonomous-driving domain benchmark on a private real-world dashcam SCDS dataset; does NOT map to standard families (not QA / multi-hop / web / embodied (ALFWorld etc.) / tool (ToolBench) / code (SWE-bench) / memory (LoCoMo) / decision-RL (D4RL)). Closest normalized label: real-world driving decision-making / risk-scenario understanding (egocentric dashcam video).
baselines: Internal comparisons rather than external SOTA methods: (1) eight open-source LLMs of varying size as backbones (Mistral 7B, Mistral-Nemo 12B, Mixtral 8x7B, Phi-4 14B, DeepSeek-R1 14B, Gemma2 27B, Qwen2.5 32B, Llama3.3 70B); (2) prompt-setting baselines: risk-unaware vs risk-aware prompting; (3) in-context-learning baselines: zero-shot vs 1/3/5-shot, and random case selection vs similarity-based (same-risk-type) CBR retrieval. The key contrast is similarity-based CBR retrieval vs random sampling and vs zero-shot.
key_metrics: Decision alignment: Micro-accuracy / micro-average accuracy of the recommended evasive maneuver vs the ground-truth human-driver maneuver. Text quality (Event Context and Ego-car Maneuver Justification, assessing interpretability / alignment with expert reasoning): BLEU-4, METEOR, ROUGE-L, CIDEr. Variances reported in brackets.
headline_result: Llama3.3-70B achieves the highest maneuver-decision accuracy: micro-accuracy 0.9412 (~0.941) under the risk-aware setting (vs 0.9369/0.937 risk-unaware); abstract/intro cite 0.9412 as the top alignment with human-like decisions. In the CBR-augmented setting, Llama3.3-70B reaches 0.94 accuracy with similarity-based 5-shot retrieval, and similarity-based case retrieval consistently outperforms random sampling across models.
ablations: Several controlled comparisons act as ablations: (Q1) vanilla LLM size comparison (8 models) showing larger instruction-tuned models do better; (Q2) risk-aware vs risk-unaware prompting (risk-aware generally improves accuracy across 5 top models, e.g., Gemma2 27B 0.893->0.918, Qwen2.5 32B 0.875->0.898, Llama3.3 70B 0.937->0.941; Phi-4 14B slightly drops, underperforming on adjacent-vehicle conflicts); (Q3) CBR augmentation ablation over selection method (random vs similarity) x shots (0/1/3/5): similarity-based selection consistently beats random; a single irrelevant (random 1-shot) example often drops below the zero-shot baseline; more similar examples monotonically help; DeepSeek-R1 is a notable exception where more few-shot examples degrade performance (consistent with the DeepSeek-R1 paper). Per-risk-type breakdowns are given in Tables 4-5.
evaluation_decoupling: Partial. Decision-outcome accuracy (maneuver micro-accuracy) is reported separately from generation-quality metrics (BLEU-4/METEOR/ROUGE-L/CIDEr on event context and justification). However, intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / retrieval precision) are NOT reported; retrieval quality is assessed only indirectly via downstream accuracy (similarity vs random selection).
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both outcome and (linguistic) process quality: the final maneuver decision is scored by accuracy (outcome), while the intermediate event-context understanding and the maneuver justification are scored with NLG metrics (a proxy for reasoning/interpretability quality). No formal step-wise reasoning-faithfulness or retrieval-accuracy metric.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Not quantified. The paper does not report retrieval-call counts, API/token cost, latency, or rollouts. Models are run locally via Ollama; the only efficiency-relevant observation is that retrieval is a single similarity pass and few-shot count (1/3/5) trades context length for accuracy, but no token/latency numbers are given. [uncertain].
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k few-shot selection: k in {1, 3, 5} same-risk-type cases injected as exemplars (best results generally at 5-shot with similarity selection, except DeepSeek-R1 which degrades with more shots). No explicit token/prompt budget is reported; k is a fixed hyperparameter, not adaptive or budget-capped. Event captions range ~115-895 tokens/words (Table 2), giving an implicit sense of per-example length. [uncertain] on exact prompt token budget.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (this is a system/method paper, not a survey).
benchmark_construction_and_size: Source: Tokyo University of Agriculture and Technology naturalistic near-miss dashcam dataset (>220,000 ~15s near-accident segments with descriptive tags). Used subset: 1000 samples balanced across 7 SCDS risk types (~143 each), each manually verified for semantic-annotation correctness and manually labeled with the ground-truth human-executed evasive maneuver (one maneuver per video from an 8-option maneuver set). Split: 900 cases as the case base, 100 (~14/type) as test queries for the CBR evaluation. Semantic annotations (risk type via a two-stage safe/risk-then-7-class predictor; event captions synthesized by DeepSeek-R1) are human-verified. Best system score (difficulty signal): up to 0.94 maneuver accuracy (Llama3.3-70B). Answer verifiability: maneuver labels are human-annotated ground truth; dataset is private/copyright-restricted, limiting reproducibility.
builds_on: Authors' prior open Case-Based Reasoning driving-assistance framework (Gan, Dao, Zettsu 2022, IEEE BigData) and their dashcam scene-understanding / risk-prediction pipeline (e.g., Drive-CLIP 2024; MM-TrafficRisk, Dao et al. 2023; SCVLM, Shi et al. 2024). Chain-of-Thought prompting (Wei et al. 2022). DeepSeek-R1 (Guo et al. 2025) for caption synthesis. nomic-embed-text embedding model. Ollama for local LLM serving. Classic CBR retrieve-reuse paradigm + LLM in-context learning / RAG.
contrasts_with: Rule-based collision-avoidance decision systems (Li et al. 2021) and end-to-end imitation/RL driving (Chen et al. 2024) lacking interpretability and long-tail robustness; prior LLM-for-driving works operating in simulators or drone-based full-observability BEV settings (DiLu/Wen et al. 2023, Fu et al. 2024; DriveMLM/Wang et al. 2023; LMDrive/Shao et al. 2024; DriveGPT4/Xu et al. 2024); knowledge/RAG-driven LLM driving methods (Cai et al. 2024 'Driving with regulation'; SafeDrive/Zhou et al. 2024; SACA/Zhao et al. 2025). CBR-LLM is positioned as egocentric dashcam (partial-observability, realistic) + experiential case retrieval, contrasting full-observability simulator/BEV approaches; and within its own experiments, similarity-based CBR retrieval is contrasted with random sampling and zero-shot, and risk-aware vs risk-unaware prompting.
lineage: Group D (case-based planning / case-based reasoning). An applied CBR+LLM decision-making system that implements Retrieve + Reuse (and a designed-but-untested Retain/evolving case base) of the CBR cycle: it uses similarity-based same-category case recall as in-context few-shot exemplars adapted by LLM Chain-of-Thought, in the safety-critical autonomous-driving domain from egocentric dashcam video. Sits in the CBR-meets-LLM-ICL line (alongside CaseGPT, CBR-RAG) but is distinguished by its multimodal video grounding, explicit risk-aware prompting, and human-experience case base, while lacking a learned retrieval policy and an experimentally evaluated case-adaptation/retention loop.
